'''Kevin Huerter''' (born August 27, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]].

==Early life and high school career==

Huerter, a 6'7" [[shooting guard]], played at [[Shenendehowa High School]] in [[Clifton Park, New York]], a suburb of [[Albany, New York|Albany]], the state capital. During his career, he led the school to its first state championship, set the state scoring record and, as a senior, was named [[Mr. New York Basketball]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Don|last=Markus|url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bal-maryland-basketball-recruit-kevin-huerter-honored-by-high-school-turning-his-likeness-into-a-logo-20160408-story.html|title=Maryland basketball signee Kevin Huerter honored by high school turning his likeness into a logo|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|date=April 8, 2016|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==

Huerter chose Maryland from over 20 offers.<ref>{{cite web|first=Brady|last=Farkas|url=http://1045theteam.com/kevin-huerter-signs-nli-with-maryland/|title=Kevin Huerter signs NLI with Maryland|work=1045theteam.com|date=November 12, 2015|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref> He earned a starting position as a freshman, averaging 9.3 points and 4.9 rebounds per game on the season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Arsenault|url=https://www.timesunion.com/sports/article/Kevin-Huerter-makes-strides-with-Maryland-12736482.php#item-85307-tbla-4|title=Kevin Huerter makes strides with Maryland basketball|work=[[Times Union (Albany)|Times Union]]|date=March 7, 2018|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref> Following his freshman season, Huerter was selected to the United States team for the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]], where the team finished third.<ref>{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Greene|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/kevin-huerter-selected-final-usa-154438945.html|title=Kevin Huerter selected to final USA U19 roster|work=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=June 22, 2017|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref>

As a sophomore, Huerter increased his production, scoring 14.8 points and averaging 5 rebounds per game. At the close of the season, he was named honorable mention All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Tyler|last=Byrum|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/maryland-terps/cowan-fernando-huerter-receive-all-big-ten-honors|title=Cowan, Fernando, Huerter receive All-Big Ten honors|work=[[NBCSports.com]]|date=February 27, 2018|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==

Following his sophomore season at Maryland, Huerter declared his eligibility for the [[2018 NBA draft]] without an agent.<ref>{{cite web|first=Don|last=Markus|url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/tracking-the-terps/bs-sp-kevin-huerter-nba-draft-0420-story.html|title=Maryland's Kevin Huerter will declare for NBA draft but will not sign with an agent|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|date=April 20, 2018|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref> He was selected to participate in the [[NBA Draft Combine]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Tyler|last=Byrum|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/maryland-terps/marylands-kevin-huerter-surprises-2018-nba-combine|title=Maryland's Kevin Huerter surprises at 2018 NBA Combine|work=[[NBCSports.com]]|date=May 17, 2018|accessdate=May 27, 2018}}</ref> After working out with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], Huerter opted to hire an agent and remain in the NBA draft, forgoing his final two years of college eligibility on May 30, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|first=Gary|last=Parrish|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/marylands-kevin-huerter-will-remain-in-the-nba-draft-dealing-a-big-blow-to-the-terrapins/|title=Maryland's Kevin Huerter will remain in the NBA Draft dealing a big blow to the Terrapins|work=[[CBSSports.com]]|date=May 30, 2018|accessdate=May 30, 2018}}</ref>
